paras: The police shooting at Roland Jones took place on the night of Monday, 21 August 1905, in Virginia, when an officer fired a pistol at Jones, a Black man, to make him stop. Jones was not reported hurt, but a false report that someone had been killed caused a stir, and the next morning he was fined $10 for beating a woman named Laura Brackett.

Jones, whom the Richmond Times-Dispatch called "a big black negro," was charged with beating Laura Brackett, whose race the paper did not give. The item names no city; it ran on the page that carried the paper's Manchester news, but the court is identified only by its justice.

On Monday night an officer, who is not named, "fired at Roland to make him stop," and Jones ran after the shot. Word spread that someone had been killed, and there was "confusion for a while." According to the paper, the rumor was fed by Simon Forsythe, who was found drunk and asleep on a secluded street shortly after the shot and could not be roused.

On the morning of 22 August Justice Crutchfield fined Jones $10, a sum the paper said "he didn't have," and gave Forsythe twenty days. No inquiry into the officer's use of his pistol appears in the coverage.

The only report found is a short item in the Times-Dispatch police-court column of 23 August, under the headline "Causes Excitement" and the subhead "Justice John Separates Darkey From Money He Didn't Have." The item treated the night as comedy, joking that Jones had offended against "the peace and dignity of the Commonwealth and Laura's head," and mentioned the gunfire only as the source of the excitement. No Black-press account of the episode was found.

quotes: Roland Jones, a big black negro, was the direct cause of a lot of excitement Monday night, and yesterday morning Justice Crutchfield separated Roland from $10 that he didn't have.
But an officer fired at Roland to make him stop, and the report became current that some one had been killed. There was confusion for a while.
The specific offense with which Roland was charged, was that of beating one Laura Brackett against the peace and dignity of the Commonwealth and Laura's head.
